title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X/S is a smooth relative curve with ω = Ω^1_{X/S} invertible, and 2 invertible on X. The neighbouring pages make clear that the object studied is a rank-2 bundle (equivalently a P^1-bundle P with a section σ) carrying a connection that is 'transversal' to the filtration. In modern terms this is an indigenous bundle, i.e. a PGL2/SL2-oper, i.e. a projective structure on X/S. These are exactly the bundles that the Gauss–Manin connection of a family of elliptic curves, or a second-order Picard–Fuchs equation, produces.

The data are:
- a line bundle Ω;
- an extension 0→Ω→L→O_X→0;
- a first-order differential operator c_Ω: Ω→L⊗ω.

The composite Ω→L⊗ω→ω is linear and an isomorphism (normalised as '-2i'). It is used to identify Ω≃ω.

On the previous page, c_Ω is factored through the universal first-order operator d^1: Ω→P^1_{X/S}(Ω). This gives a linear map γ: P^1(Ω)→L⊗ω, which is a morphism of extensions inducing Id on Ω⊗ω and -2 on the quotient. With 2 invertible and c transversal, γ is an isomorphism.

This page draws the consequences.
1. Twisting by ω^{-1} and using Ω≃ω gives L ≃ P^1_{X/S}(ω)⊗ω^{-1}. The right side is the Atiyah extension of O_X by ω attached to the line bundle ω.
2. Diagram (*): the isomorphism is a map of extensions 0→ω→L→O_X→0 to 0→ω→P^1(ω)ω^{-1}→O_X→0, inducing id on ω and -2 on O_X.
3. Diagram (**): rescaling by -1/2 gives -1/2 on ω and id on O_X.
4. Hence the ω-torsors (extension classes in H^1(X,ω)) of L and of P^1(ω)ω^{-1} differ by the factor -2. So the class of L is -1/2 times the Atiyah class of ω, i.e. the Atiyah class of a putative ω^{-1/2}. This is the familiar fact that the oper bundle is J^1(K^{-1/2}), here formulated without choosing a theta-characteristic.
5. Under these identifications, the restriction c|Ω, Ω≃ω→L⊗ω≃P^1(ω), is identified with the universal operator d^1_{ω,X/S}.
6. NB: one restricts to connections c: V→V⊗ω whose restriction to Ω≃ω is d^1_{ω,X/S}. These are determined modulo sections of Ω⊗ω≃ω^{⊗2}.

The next page confirms the conclusion: such connections form a torsor under ω^{⊗2}. That is the classical statement that projective structures / sl2-opers form an affine space over quadratic differentials. A boxed margin there says that giving c_Ω amounts to identifying the second-order infinitesimal neighbourhoods of σ(X) in P and of the diagonal in X×_S X. A further note plans to compare the formal completion of P along σ with P^∞_Δ.

Purpose: a characteristic-free, square-root-free algebraic description of indigenous bundles / projective structures. This is preparation for relating Gauss–Manin connections (e.g. of H^1_dR of elliptic families, with Kodaira–Spencer) to second-order Picard–Fuchs operators, and presumably to Cartier/Frobenius in characteristic p (the dossier title).
errors: No substantive mathematical error. The factor -2 on the quotient becomes, after rescaling, -1/2 on the sub. This is consistent, and so is the statement that the extension classes differ by multiplication by -2.

The normalisation '-2i' (or '-2id') is convention-dependent and the signs are hard to read. The hypothesis '2 invertible' is genuinely needed for γ to be an isomorphism. The margin of the next page ('est-il vraiment nécessaire?') shows Grothendieck himself questioning this; in characteristic 2 the statement fails as formulated.

ideas.what: Rank-2 bundle (P^1-bundle with section) with transversal connection on a relative curve; second fundamental form Ω ≃ ω
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (1967); Beilinson–Drinfeld (opers, 1990s); Mochizuki (p-adic Teichmüller, 1990s) in arbitrary characteristic

ideas.what: Identification of the oper extension L with the Atiyah/jet extension P^1(ω)⊗ω^{-1}, the class of L being -1/2 times the Atiyah class of ω (avoiding a choice of ω^{1/2})
ideas.modern_name: oper bundle ≃ J^1(K^{-1/2}); Atiyah class of a line bundle via first principal parts
ideas.usually_credited_to: Atiyah (1957) for the Atiyah extension; folklore / Beilinson–Drinfeld for the oper statement

ideas.what: Connections extending the fixed c|Ω form a torsor under ω^{⊗2}
ideas.modern_name: affine space of projective structures / opers modelled on quadratic differentials
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Gunning, Hubbard); algebraic form by Beilinson–Drinfeld, Mochizuki

ideas.what: Universal first-order differential operator d^1: M→P^1_{X/S}(M), used to linearise first-order operators

missed.claim: Grothendieck worked out, apparently around 1972, a characteristic-free, theta-characteristic-free algebraic theory of indigenous bundles (sl2-opers) over a general base S. This includes the torsor under ω^{⊗2} and the description via second-order infinitesimal neighbourhoods. It sits in a dossier together with the Cartier operator, anticipating the setting of Mochizuki's p-adic Teichmüller theory (indigenous bundles + Frobenius) by two decades. This is a historical priority/context point, not a new theorem.
missed.quote: Elle sont déterminés modulo sections de Ω⊗ω ≃ ω^{⊗2}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents unpublished early work by Grothendieck on algebraic opers/projective structures in mixed characteristic contexts. Of interest to historians of p-adic Teichmüller theory and opers; the mathematics itself is now standard.

missed.claim: The planned comparison of the oper data (P,σ,c) with the formal neighbourhood identification O_{\hat P} ≅ P^∞_Δ is left undone. This would be an all-orders version of the statement that a projective structure identifies the formal neighbourhood of the section with that of the diagonal.
missed.quote: Faire le lien avec la filtration (P,σ,c) et les divers formules O_{\hat P}≅P^∞_Δ (next page)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Known in spirit (projective structures as formal coordinate data). An explicit treatment over general bases with 2 invertible is routine, so this is of minor interest.

deep.surprise_reason: Clean, correct algebraic treatment of indigenous bundles / opers predating the usual algebraic references, but the results (jet description, ω^{⊗2}-torsor) are classical and well established today. The interest is mainly historical.
transcription_corrections: '∘ → ω → L → O_X → 0' in (*): the first term is 0, not ∘.
'c_1Ω≃ω s'identifie' should read 'c|Ω ≃ ω' (restriction of c to Ω), not a Chern class.
'Lie V = L^{dt}' is more plausibly 'Fil. V = L' (the filtration piece of V), with a small annotation below; 'Lie' is doubtful.
'en [?] [?], la multiplication par -1/2' is likely 'en composant avec la multiplication par -1/2' (or similar).

In the parenthetical: '(Donc les torseurs sous ω≃Ω définis par l'ext. L et par l'ext. P^1_{X/S}(ω)ω^{-1} de O_X par ω (ou P^1_{X/S}(ω) de ω par ω^2) [se déduisent l'un de l'autre] par multiplication par -2)'.
